title: How a walkthrough gets from the agent to your screen

segments.narration: Everything starts in the MCP server's entry point. {a}The agent calls present_walkthrough with a finished script, {b}and the first thing we do is resolve it against the repo.

actions.match: const result = await resolveScript(ws, { title, segments }

segments.narration: Resolution lives in script dot t s. {a}For every action we check the file exists, and {b}symbol anchors get looked up with tree-sitter, so the agent can't point at code that isn't there.
The symbol table itself comes from {a}this outline function. It walks the syntax tree and records every class, function and method with its line range.
Once the script is valid, the hub sends it to the browser and {a}blocks until something happens: the walkthrough finishes, or you pause and ask a question.
On the browser side, the player speaks each segment and {a}fires actions as the voice reaches their markers. If an animation is still running, {b}it holds the voice until the screen catches up.

actions.match: // Hold the voice until the earlier action finishes.
